painters.name: Gan-Erdene.Ts
awards: Cultural Ambassador of Mongolia to the Federal Republic of Germany, Cultural Leading Worker
painters.bio:
GAN-ERDENE TSEND
born in 1979 in Mörön, Mongolia. He studied at the University of Fine Arts in Ulaanbaatar (1996-2001) and at the Academy of Fine Arts in Münster, Germany (2003-2010) where he has lived and worked ever since.
Gan-Erdene Tsend’s paintings are characterised by the vastness and seemingly endless landscape of Mongolia. His motifs often depict the barren rocky environment of the Mongolian steppe – mostly deserted and viewed from a bird’s-eye perspective, often without a visible sky. Despite this reduction the influences of sun, wind, and the shifting shadows of clouds are clearly noticeable in his paintings. The mountain ranges seem to breathe lending the works a quiet meditative presence. Some of the works were created using felt. “They all tell of nomadic culture and endless landscapes as well as the nomads’ deep spiritual respect for nature and the enduring traditions that have existed in Mongolian nomadic culture for over a thousand years and are still preserved today,” says the artist about his paintings.
Gan-Erdene´s oil painting “Heimweg” (Way home (many variations)) depicts a landscape that springs from the artist’s imagination but could actually exist both, in reality and in the viewer’s imagination. The landscape depicted is barren with a path in the middle that disappears into the horizon. The seemingly endless expanse of desert and steppe clearly references the artist’s Mongolian roots. Although the landscape depicted is deserted, traces of human activity are nevertheless visible: plastic bottles, coffee cups, empty cola cans, and plastic bags are scattered on and off the path, illustrating the impact of consumer culture on the environment. While the viewer’s gaze is initially drawn to the path in the centre of the picture from a distance, the disturbing details of the field of rubbish only become apparent upon closer inspection.

painters.name: Bazarvaani.S
painters.bio: Bazarvaan was born in 1982 in Uliastai, Zavkhan province. From 1999 to 2002, he studied at the Rajiv Gandhi School of Art and Handcrafts, and later at the School of Fine Arts, Mongolian State University of Arts and Culture from 2003 to 2008.
painters.statement:
Bazarvaan regularly participates in both national and international exhibitions. His works have been showcased in Golden Brush, Spring, Grand Art, Nude Art, as well as in exhibitions such as Mongolia on Horseback, Etugen Tenger, and Best Work of the Year. He fascinated with horses since childhood, his paintings are related in neo-realism, often infused with elements of impressionism.
His art transports viewers into a world of horses — at times serene and still, at times powerful and galloping with unbridled energy.
awards: Member of the Union of Mongolian Artists

painters.name: Narangerel.Ts
painters.bio:
Artist Narangerel was born in 1956 in Ulaanbaatar. He studied monumental painting at the Academy of Arts, Architecture and Design in Prague. He worked at the Union of Mongolian Artists and served for many years as a professor and dean at the Institute of Fine Arts.
Since 1974, he has presented both solo and group exhibitions in Mongolia, USA, Turkey, China, Germany, France, Japan, and other countries, gaining recognition in the international art world. His awards include the Honored Awardee of the Union of Mongolian Artists (1991), Cultural Leading Worker (2002), and an Honored Artists of Mongolia (2012), among many others.

painters.name: Bold.D
painters.bio:
Do. Bold, People’s Artist of Mongolia and a prominent representative of modern Mongolian fine arts, is renowned for capturing the harmony of colors, poetic composition, and the profound emotions of nature, history, and the human spirit in his works.
Born in Khövsgöl Province, he studied at the Repin Academy of Fine Arts and has since introduced the unique essence of Mongolian art to international audiences. His works have been exhibited in Austria, Japan, the United States, Germany, and other countries.
In recognition of his remarkable artistic achievements, he was awarded the State Prize of Mongolia in 1994 and the title of People’s Artist in 2012. His creations resonate deeply with the soul, heart, and spirit of Mongolia.
Visit our gallery to experience the remarkable works of the distinguished artist who first introduced contemporary art to Mongolia.

painters.name: Tumurbaatar.S
painters.bio: Tumurbaatar, distinguished representative and educator in Mongolian fine arts, began his artist career in 1978. He was the first to initiate and establish the monumental painting program in Mongolia, developing its curriculum and training numerous talented artists. He dedicated 38 years of his career to the University of Arts and Culture (SUIS) and also served as the Director of the Union of Mongolian Artists (UMA) for 8 years, making invaluable contributions to the development of Mongolian fine arts. He served as the lead designer of the decorative project for the Chinggis Khaan Museum. In recognition of his artistic achievements and dedication, he was honored with the title of Cultural Leading Worker (1999), the Medal of Honor for Labor (2002), the Medal of Altan gadas (2012), the Order of the Red Banner of Labor Merit (2017), and the prestigious title of Honored Artists of Mongolia (2025). We warmly invite you to visit our gallery and experience the unique talent and creative imagination embodied in the works of Tumurbaatar, a distinguished representative and esteemed teacher of Mongolian fine arts.

painters.name: Davaasambuu.T
painters.bio:
Davaasambuu is a talented sculptor who has created a distinctive and innovative presence in the field of contemporary Mongolian sculpture. He graduated from the Mongolian University of Arts and Culture in 2009, and from the Mongolian National University of Education in 2012, and is currently pursuing a doctoral degree in Art Studies.
Since 2010, he has been working as a sculpture lecturer, making significant contributions to guiding the younger generation. His works have been successfully showcased at international exhibitions in Germany, China, South Korea, Taiwan, Bangladesh, the United Kingdom, and other countries, with several pieces now preserved in national museums and state collections.

painters.name: Batogtokh.T
painters.style: Sculpture, craftsman, visual thinking, music and performing arts
painters.bio:
Artist Battogtokh is a multitalented artist who has made a significant contribution to contemporary Mongolian visual art by integrating sculpture, visual thinking, music, and performing arts. Trained as a sculptor and later educated as an opera singer, he has developed a distinctive artistic language, philosophy, and mode of expression.
His solo and group exhibitions have been held in Mongolia, the United Kingdom, Poland, South Korea, Japan, Italy, China, and Germany. He has consistently participated in an international exhibitions and art festivals such as Nord Art, Incheon Art Festival, UB Art Fair, and Etugen, earning wide recognition for his work.
Battogtokh is particularly known for his sculptural works carved from animal shoulder bones. Through these materials, he reinterprets traditional symbolism, mythology, and the inner world of human existence within the context of contemporary art, expressing nomadic philosophy through intricate craftsmanship and multilayered meanings.
Preserving the natural form of the material, his works demonstrate exceptional carving skills and profound artistic sensitivity, embodying a harmonious fusion of cultural heritage and contemporary artistic expression.

painters.name: Ser-Od.G
painters.bio:
Artist Ser-Od was born in 1993 in Zavkhan Province, Mongolia. He is a representative of the younger generation of artists actively contributing to the field of contemporary Mongolian fine art. From 2011 to 2015, he studied painting at the School of Fine Arts of the Mongolian State University of Culture and Arts. Since 2015, he has been working as an exhibition organizer at the Union of Mongolian Artists while pursuing his own artistic practice, regularly participating in many national and international exhibitions.
His works are characterized by a strong conceptual approach that interweaves Mongolian nomadic life, equestrian culture, nature, and cosmic symbolism.

painters.name: Sukh-Bat.M
painters.bio:
Sh.Sukhbat is a contemporary Mongolian artist. He graduated from the School of Fine Arts at the Mongolian University of Arts and Culture and earned his Master’s degree in 2014. Since 2017, he has been working as an independent artist.
His works explore the vast sense of the steppe, historical memory, and inner moments of emotion through a contemporary visual language. He has participated in many national and international exhibitions and held his solo exhibition “Moment” in 2019.
